historical_references.context: Ibn Khaldun mentions a Berber chief named Syauqi bin al-Hasan, ruler of the Maghrib during the early 14th century. He was a vassal of the Hafsid emir of Tunis, Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad II, and was known for his military prowess and successful campaigns against the Marinids and other enemies.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Battuta's 'Rihla', Volume 1, page 149 The name Syauqi carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ibn Battuta, the famous traveler, visited the court of Syauqi bin 'Umar, who was the ruler of the Emirate of Tlemcen in the western Maghrib around 1352. Ibn Battuta recounts Syauqi's generosity and his military conquests in the region.
